name: Longview Philanthropy (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Moves money: each area its directed money goes to, read live, brings its own countries.
summary: Longview Philanthropy advises major donors on reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI, nuclear weapons and biological threats, recommends grants and runs regranting funds; this model covers its US and UK entities' 2025 operating costs ($6.9M; the grants they passed on are the grantees' cost). At the defaults it averts about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000: of the $27M donors gave through its funds, the site's shared share for a meta charity without a donor survey credits it with causing 30%, and of the roughly $28M more it says its advice directed from donors' own foundations the same share counts as redirected, valued only for the gain over an ordinary charity of the same areas and discounted for missing data (the one branch so discounted); each dollar is valued at the site's AI (81% of the money, our blend of its itemised grants and a judgment), nuclear (12%) and biosecurity (3%) charities. The result moves most with where shifted money would otherwise have gone, the share that went to nuclear work, the discount rate and the next dollar (36% of the 2025 average).

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

rows.label: Longview Philanthropy USA: its largest grant abroad, 'general support' to one recipient in Europe, 2025 (US$)

source.title: Longview Philanthropy USA Inc. (EIN 93-2664730), Form 990 for the year ended 31 December 2025 (IRS e-file; its financial statements audited)
source.page: Schedule F Part II, first row

rows.explainer: One grant of $5.69M to an organisation in Europe, unnamed (Schedule F gives regions only). If it went to Longview's own UK company, the UK's grants would re-grant it and count it twice; see the next row.

rows.label: Share of that grant that went to Longview's own UK company (and so is counted again in the UK's grants)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 5% (0% to 50%). Schedule F calls the grant 'general support', which would have reached the UK company as unrestricted income, and the UK company's unrestricted donations in 2025 were £2,054 (note 2, p. 13); the US Form 990 files no Schedule R (no related organisations in 2025), the UK accounts report no related-party transactions besides directors' pay (note 13, p. 17), and the US entity became the UK company's member only in October 2026 (Companies House resolution, 13 October 2026). A transfer recorded as restricted income under another label is still possible, given the grant's size and region, so the range runs to half of it.

rows.label: Grants both entities paid from their funds and restricted gifts, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: The US and UK grants (the UK's at the 2025 rate), less any part of the US grant to Europe that went to the UK company, so no dollar is counted twice.

rows.label: Donations to its Emerging Challenges Fund through Giving What We Can, 2025 (US$)

source.title: Longview Philanthropy, Join 2,000+ people donating through the ECF (EA Forum, 19 November 2025)

rows.explainer: Donations to Longview's public fund are donations to Giving What We Can, which pays the grantees on Longview's recommendations ('All funds are disbursed based on recommendations by Longview Philanthropy', fund page disclosures), so they aren't in either entity's books. The 2025 donations stand in for the fund's 2025 grants (six grants, in its 2025 report, which can't be opened without sign-in); the fund closed to new donations in 2026. Donations to the Nuclear Weapons Policy Fund through Giving What We Can are not published and sit in the advised remainder below.

rows.label: Money donors gave through Longview's funds that reached grantees, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Grants from its own books plus the Emerging Challenges Fund's donations: money donors handed to Longview to grant. The grants are the year's flow to grantees, against the year's cost (Convention 3).

rows.label: Share of the money given through its funds that Longview caused
rows.explainer: Longview publishes no survey of its donors: the shared figure for a meta charity without one (30%, 15% to 45%, from Giving What We Can's donor surveys). Its donors are a few large givers already committed to these risks, who would mostly have given anyway, some to the same organisations.

rows.label: Money moved through its funds that Longview caused, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Donations through its funds × the share it caused; the new-money share and where shifted money would have gone are applied in the shared rows.

rows.label: Money Longview says it directed in 2025, funds and advice together (US$)

source.title: Longview Philanthropy, Join 2,000+ people donating through the ECF (EA Forum, 19 November 2025)
source.quote: Longview has directed over $50 million in 2025.
source.note: Stated on 19 November 2025, six weeks before the year's end; the post adds that its 'private and public funds and bespoke advisory services' supported 'more than 50 projects'. LongtermWiki gives the same figure ('$50M+ in 2025'). The annual report sits in a Google Drive file that can't be opened without sign-in.

rows.explainer: Its own figure, 'over $50 million' by mid-November 2025: $55M ($50M to $65M) for the full year, our estimate allowing for year-end giving. It includes the grants from its funds counted above and the giving donors made from their own foundations and funds on its recommendations.

rows.label: Money donors gave from their own vehicles on Longview's recommendations, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: The directed total less the money through its funds: grants major donors made themselves after its advice, plus any Nuclear Weapons Policy Fund donations made through Giving What We Can (not published, so they can't be moved to the fund money). The funds' money is an audited count, so the remainder is never below $23M.

rows.label: Share of the advised money whose destination Longview's advice changed
rows.explainer: No survey of the donors it advises: the site's shared figure for a meta charity without one (30%, 15% to 45%), read as the share of the advised money whose destination its advice changed. None of it counts as new money: the people it advises are existing givers of $1M or more a year who were giving anyway (templates.md: advice that changes where money is spent is all shifted); new philanthropists drawn in by its convenings are in the side effects.

rows.label: Advised money whose allocation its advice changed, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Giving that would have happened anyway but went elsewhere because of its advice: all shifted money, valued in the shared rows by the gain over where it would have gone (informed_money_value).

rows.label: Money moved or changed per dollar of Longview's costs
rows.explainer: For reading only: the money it caused or redirected per dollar it spent.

rows.label: Value per unit affected per year, in units of value
rows.explainer: Unused: the policy branch is 0 (units_affected_per_year), so this row multiplies nothing. It keeps the template's figure and range only so the canonical row exists; changing it moves no result.

rows.label: Probability the change happens because of this work
rows.explainer: Unused: the policy branch is 0 (units_affected_per_year), so this row multiplies nothing. It keeps the template's figure and range only so the canonical row exists; changing it moves no result.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: Unused: the policy branch is 0, so this row discounts nothing; kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.label: Years from the win until the policy takes effect
rows.explainer: Unused: the policy branch is 0 (units_affected_per_year), so this row multiplies nothing. It keeps the template's figure and range only so the canonical row exists; changing it moves no result.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the policy takes effect
rows.explainer: Unused: the policy branch is 0, so this row discounts nothing; kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.label: Discounted years of impact
rows.explainer: Unused: the policy branch is 0, so this row discounts nothing; kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.label: Expected value of the policy or research (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: 0: the policy branch is empty (Longview wins nothing of its own; its value is the money it directs).

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity: about half the money moved wouldn't otherwise have been given (Ambitious Impact's Effective Giving Incubation report), from 35% to 80%.

rows.label: Value of a dollar to global health and poverty charities (GiveWell's Top Charities, live), units of value
rows.explainer: GiveWell's four Top Charities (Against Malaria Foundation, Malaria Consortium, Helen Keller Intl, New Incentives), each at GiveWell's figure for the charity on the rankings (its programmes and locations weighted by funding) under your values, weighted by what GiveWell directed to each in 2024 (50%, 29%, 18%, 4%).

rows.label: Value of a dollar to the causes Longview directs money to (live), units of value
rows.explainer: Where its directed money went in 2025, by area (our judgment, a dollar-weighted blend of its itemised US grants and a judged split of the rest, facts/meta.json longview_2025_share_*: AI 81%, nuclear 12%, biosecurity 3%), each area at its charities' figures on the rankings under your values (#cause:ai, #cause:nuclear, #cause:biosecurity, equal weights), by the site's rule for a split (normalization.md 2.8). Every itemised grantee with a model here is read at its own live result for its share of the AI grants: MATS (21%) and METR (3.4%); the other grantees and the money no list itemises take their area's charities. Digital sentience (its Digital Sentience Fund and two US grants), a cause with no model here, and Rethink Priorities' grant (a money mover) drop out at the average of the rest.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where this organisation's money went: its own published split, each recipient at its live result on this site (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: an ordinary charity of each cause its money goes to, in its own mix), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the shared rule for an organisation whose money goes to several causes. Shifted money would have gone to an ordinary charity of the same cause: each cause's at the rule for a mover in that cause (GiveDirectly's live result, times a shared multiple, 1×, from 0 to 3×, over the global-health charities' on the rankings, times that cause's charities'), weighted by the organisation's own split, all live under your values.

rows.label: Value of a dollar all shifted (given anyway, now to a better use), units of value
rows.explainer: Money that would have been given or spent anyway counts only for the gain over where it would have gone: a grantmaker's grants, or spending that research or advice changed.

rows.label: Value of the spending its research or advice changed (all shifted money), units of value
rows.explainer: Spending its research or advice changed, at a judged share of the money it informed: all of it would have been spent anyway, so it counts for the gain over where it would have gone, discounted for weak evidence and for an outcome not measured for this charity (docs/normalization.md 2.8, 2.12).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone.

rows.label: Side effects of the money directed, as a share of its value
rows.explainer: Good and harm of Longview's own beyond the money counted: its convenings and donor education draw new philanthropists to these risks and its grant reports inform other funders (positive); a few advisers steering much of a field's private money narrows its views and its bets (negative). The grantees' own chance of backfiring is in their figures already. 5% (−5% to +20%) of the modelled value, our judgment, with no reference class.

rows.label: Value of the money Longview moved and changed (units of value)
rows.explainer: Fund money it caused, net of where shifted money would have gone (new money in full), plus advised money its advice redirected, all shifted, after the evidence and missing-data steps; with the side effects.

rows.label: Careers changed per year
rows.explainer: 0: Longview moves money, not people; the fellowships and training programmes it funds (MATS, Neuromatch, Scoville fellows) are its grantees' work, inside their figures.

rows.label: Pay a career changer gives up per year (US$)
rows.explainer: The site's shared default (facts/meta.json) while careers_changed is 0: Longview changes no careers, so this multiplies nothing.

rows.label: Years a career changer stays in high-impact work
rows.explainer: The site's shared default (facts/meta.json) while careers_changed is 0: Longview changes no careers, so this multiplies nothing.

rows.label: Years a career changer stays, discounted
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Value of a dollar of the new employers' work (units of value)
rows.explainer: Unused while careers_changed is 0; it reads the destinations the money goes to.

rows.label: Share of the career changes the charity caused
rows.explainer: The site's shared default (facts/meta.json) while careers_changed is 0: Longview changes no careers, so this multiplies nothing.

rows.label: Value of one career change (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one career-change step (docs/normalization.md 2.8).

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Unused: no careers changed (careers_changed is 0), so this row multiplies nothing; kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.label: Value of the career changes (units of value)
rows.explainer: Unused while careers_changed is 0: the site's career-change step, kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: Applies to the advised money its advice changed (informed_money_value) and to the empty policy branch: how far the redirected giving does what its area's charities on the rankings do, given that nobody measures what its advice changed or how its grantees compare with the ranked ones. 0.7 (0.5 to 0.9), the template's figure.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 1: what would have happened anyway is asked once, in the money rows (the share of fund money it caused, the share of advised money its advice changed, new against shifted money); the policy branch it would apply to is empty.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: 1: the grantees' own costs and co-funders are inside each destination's figure per dollar; the policy branch is empty.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: The site's missing-data discount (Convention 12): what Longview's advice changed is judged, not counted, so the advised branch is thin; the money through its funds is counted and takes no discount.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Total value (units of value)
rows.explainer: The adjustments apply to the empty policy branch; the money moved carries its own steps (own effect, new money, the advised branch's evidence and missing-data steps).

rows.label: Value per dollar
rows.explainer: For WELLBYs, rename the uov_* rows to wellbys_* and report in wellby. For animals, rename them to sads_* and add the species section of the corporate-campaign template (output ced_per_donor_dollar). For climate, start from the climate skeleton.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Both entities' staff pay over their operating costs (Convention 1).

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: The shared gap between what research and policy staff earn at a non-profit and what they could earn elsewhere (@staff_pay.gap_research_policy, {{row:salary_gap}}): Longview's grantmakers and advisers come from foundations, finance and government, where pay is higher.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff (in-kind donation)
How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Longview's own figure (facts/next_dollar.json): {{row:marginal_vs_past_average}} (15–75%). The result is its 2025 average, the year its grants rose fivefold with its new private AI fund; it holds over a year and a half of operating costs unrestricted, and the next dollar of advising reaches donors further from its circle.

rows.label: Your dollar's share of the cost
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources: staff's forgone pay and the new money its fund donors gave share the outcome with your dollar (the shared meta formula); advised money, all shifted, adds no resources.
